instrument.name: Timed Up and Down Stairs
instrument.primary_score: elapsed seconds for a protocol-defined stair ascent-and-descent task

original_2004.population: typically developing children and children with motor disabilities
original_2004.purpose: preliminary reliability and validity of functional stair mobility
original_2004.citation: Zaino CA, Marchese VG, Westcott SL. Pediatr Phys Ther. 2004;16(2):90-98

cp_2022.population: children with cerebral palsy aged 3-9 years
cp_2022.protocol_example: 10-step staircase in the published study; this is a study-specific configuration, not a universal TUDS standard
cp_2022.key_message: published evidence supports reliability in this population while preserving protocol-specific interpretation

normative_2021.key_message: age, height and weight contribute to expected TUDS performance; normative equations are population- and protocol-specific

rights.basis: TUDS is a timed performance procedure rather than a fixed questionnaire. Rawafid publishes an original timing/QC sheet and independently worded protocol fields; it does not reproduce a third-party form, scripted instruction set, training material, normative table or copyrighted layout.

arabic.rawafid_language_status: Original Arabic operational recording sheet; no official/validated Arabic TUDS form is claimed.
